title: Parcel Paradox
hook: Pack a tiny delivery crate where magical parcels change the rules of their neighbours: a snow globe cools one square, a sleepy dragon warms two, and the customer's promise must survive the trip.
audience: Players who enjoy tactile organizing puzzles and short, readable logic challenges without a timer.
core_loop: Read three illustrated delivery conditions, drag and rotate six parcels into a small crate, preview neighbour effects, dispatch, then improve the packing or try the next rule combination.

score_notes.demand: An established paid organizing-puzzle comparable exists; demand for magical packing has not been measured.
score_notes.distinctiveness: Visible interactions between parcels could separate this from pure spatial tidying; close packing competitors still need a deliberate search.
score_notes.fun_potential: The prediction/reveal loop is a hypothesis, with no playable test.
score_notes.scope_fit: One reusable board and six object rules bound the proposed prototype; commercial level authoring may still dominate effort.
score_notes.distribution: Packing consequences could read in a short clip, but no audience test or channel access has been demonstrated.

evidence.claim: The inspected Steam listing presents a released, purchasable organizing puzzle game with visible user review activity. This establishes a comparable, not sales or demand for this proposal.
The developer describes drag-and-drop puzzles, multiple solutions, illustration and sound design. This is a reminder that puzzle content and sensory polish need effort even when controls are simple.

risks: This may overlap closely with existing packing or inventory puzzles; originality and the working title are not cleared.
Icon-heavy rules may be hard to read without text, color-independent cues and a useful preview.
A small set of rules may exhaust its interesting combinations quickly; handcrafted content is a potential production cost.
A known competitor's reception does not establish willingness to pay for our concept.
next_test: If authorized, build one greybox crate with six parcels and three contracts. Observe five target players for ten minutes each. Continue only if at least four predict a neighbour effect without coaching after the introduction and at least three voluntarily try another contract; otherwise simplify rules or hold. These are directional discovery thresholds, not statistical market validation.
decision_reason: Held after the expanded comparison found strong packing/adjacency overlap and no independent trend origin. Preserve the pilot idea; no game selected.
commercial_hypothesis: Test a small premium PC puzzle package with a sample puzzle/demo. An initial USD 3.99-5.99 price question is an assumption to test against finished content, not a launch recommendation.

prototype_envelope.scope: One crate, six parcel types, three authored contracts, undo and effect preview; no campaign or online service.

budget_note: Unvalidated prototype planning estimate only; excludes participant recruitment and full production, art/audio, marketing, storefront work and release calendar lead time. No spend authorized.

decision_history.reason: Created as one of three varied research examples; next game remains undecided.
